director.chapterArc: A night-long ordeal begins in bodily depletion and quiet siege, turns through Katori’s humbling admission and Callie’s practical discovery of how to set the Ward down, releases into touch, water, and fragile recovery, then broadens into the material consequences of the fight: ash, debt, the lost mule, Duchess’s injury, and two emptied doors. The chapter closes by converting relief into partnership and a new logistical threat—the scarp.
director.restraintNote: Keep Original Calder grounded and physically exact. Let exhaustion slow the opening without making it languid; keep the barrow mechanics completely intelligible. Relief should arrive through cold, wet boots, touch, and water—not uplift. Tears, the mule entry, and Katori’s partnership stay unsentimental. Ash and the doors are practical facts, never mystical spectacle. Return fully to base after every cue.

cues.delivery: Carry the threat as cumulative bodily failure: deliberate counting, dulled sensation, and shaking effort, with no panic or acceleration.
cues.from: By first light the cold had reached the middle of her chest, and she had stopped being able to spit.
cues.through: Somewhere around the twentieth she had stopped being able to feel her feet. Somewhere around the twenty-fourth she had put the hook over a husk's shoulder and pulled, and nothing had happened. She had simply stood there holding the pull with her arms shaking, and the husk had leaned against the thing closed over her and gone on leaning, until Katori came out of the doorway with her Ember still buttoned inside her coat and put a boot into the back of the husk's knee and it went down.
cues.reason: The siege is established through depletion rather than overt emotion.

cues.delivery: Make the admission plain and costly; Katori relinquishes certainty without asking to be forgiven.
cues.from: "I was wrong," said Katori.
cues.through: "I was wrong," said Katori.
cues.reason: Her status shifts from unquestioned teacher toward honest partner.

cues.delivery: Keep the strange term clinical, then let the apology and offer of shared work carry sober responsibility rather than reassurance.
cues.from: "There's a word for it," said Katori. "Old women use it. I've heard it said maybe twice in my life, and both times it was said the way you'd talk about a calf with two heads. Twin-kindled. That's all it means. Two doors at once, at the start, from two different places. I've never met one. I don't know anybody who has." She pulled her cap down another half inch. "So I'm not going to tell you what it means, because I don't know. I'm not going to tell you it's rare, because rare is a word for things people have counted, and nobody's counted this. I'm going to tell you I was wrong, and I'm sorry, and that you're going to have to work some of this out with me instead of from me."

cues.reason: The chapter’s central relationship changes here.

cues.delivery: A weakened, searching explanation assembled from bodily memory; protect the pause around the yoke realization.
cues.from: "On the causeway," she said. "When the horse kicked. Before it hit. It went down, and then something — it was like something took the other side of the yoke."
cues.through: "On the causeway," she said. "When the horse kicked. Before it hit. It went down, and then something — it was like something took the other side of the yoke."
cues.reason: Callie first articulates the true mechanism.

cues.delivery: Follow the remembered strapping with exact physical placement; land the final admission as the quiet horror of an unbroken thirteen-hour effort.
cues.from: "The barrow. On the way south. I had the strapping crossed over here." Callie lifted a hand that she could not feel and drew two lines across her own chest, over her coat, over the air a finger off her coat. "Four hundred miles. And when the horse kicked, it was like somebody got in on the other side of the yoke and pulled with me. And we've been pulling ever since. Both of us. All night." She stopped. "I've never stopped. I've never set it down."
cues.through: "The barrow. On the way south. I had the strapping crossed over here." Callie lifted a hand that she could not feel and drew two lines across her own chest, over her coat, over the air a finger off her coat. "Four hundred miles. And when the horse kicked, it was like somebody got in on the other side of the yoke and pulled with me. And we've been pulling ever since. Both of us. All night." She stopped. "I've never stopped. I've never set it down."
cues.reason: The solution becomes visible through the cost.

cues.delivery: Treat every movement as a fatigued experiment that may fail. Keep buckle, weight, hips, and yoke spatially precise; suppress hope until the load localizes.
cues.from: She backed into the barrow the way she had backed into it every morning since the spring. She lifted the strapping and brought it over her shoulders and crossed it over her chest. The webbing lay a finger's width off her coat all the way round, on the air, where the Ward was. She reached behind her for the buckle, and got it, and it took her a long time with hands she could not feel.
cues.through: She felt it happen. She felt it the way you feel a second person take the far handle of a stretcher. All night the Ward had been lying on her everywhere at once, from boots to crown. Now it was not everywhere any more. It was there, in the yoke, across her chest, pulling with her. It was the same thing she had felt in the half-second before the kick, the other side of the yoke taken up.
cues.reason: This is the tense mechanical test on which survival turns.

cues.delivery: Discover ordinary air and dew as newly astonishing physical facts; brighten sensation without making the release magical or triumphant.
cues.from: The first thing she felt was the air.
cues.through: The second thing she felt was the dew.
cues.reason: Contact with the real world returns after thirteen hours of isolation.

cues.delivery: Let the tears be an involuntary bodily discharge, not performed sorrow; remain clear on the wet boots and restored feeling.
cues.from: She had walked six steps off the dry place into wet gravel. Her boots were wet. Her boots were wet and she could feel them being wet. She stood there in the road with the strapping hanging off her shoulders, feeling her own feet get cold, and she started to cry and couldn't stop, and she didn't try to.
cues.through: She had walked six steps off the dry place into wet gravel. Her boots were wet. Her boots were wet and she could feel them being wet. She stood there in the road with the strapping hanging off her shoulders, feeling her own feet get cold, and she started to cry and couldn't stop, and she didn't try to.
cues.reason: Relief finally escapes the chapter’s restraint through the body.

cues.delivery: Close and steady into her hair, repeating the fact until Callie can trust it; no celebratory lift.
cues.from: "There," said Katori, into her hair. "There. You're off. You're off it."
cues.through: "There," said Katori, into her hair. "There. You're off. You're off it."
cues.reason: Katori confirms that the ordeal is truly over.

cues.delivery: Hold the intimacy in the trembling thumb and the long silence. Let the mother’s recovered composure contain what neither of them says.
cues.from: It was the dry rough skin at the tip of the thumb along her cheekbone, and warm, and a little shaking. Her mother held it there. Callie shut her eyes and leaned her face into it and neither of them said anything for a long time.
cues.through: "Here I am."
cues.reason: Their restored physical contact is the emotional center of the recovery.

cues.delivery: Pell uses dry logistics to regulate panic; keep the joke nearly level and chiefly concerned with preventing another problem.
cues.from: "I know you don't. I'd prefer you not to be sick anyway. Otto's already done it once and I'd rather not start a fashion."
cues.through: "I know you don't. I'd prefer you not to be sick anyway. Otto's already done it once and I'd rather not start a fashion."
cues.reason: Understatement briefly releases pressure without breaking the scene’s exhaustion.

cues.delivery: Make the change minute, deep, and materially specific—the bare difference between absolute emptiness and an inch of water.
cues.from: Then, very far down, at the bottom of the place she had found in the night, something was damp that had been dry. It was not warm. It was not strength. It was the difference between a dry well and a well with an inch of water in the bottom of it. It wasn't much. But it was a long way from nothing.
cues.through: Then, very far down, at the bottom of the place she had found in the night, something was damp that had been dry. It was not warm. It was not strength. It was the difference between a dry well and a well with an inch of water in the bottom of it. It wasn't much. But it was a long way from nothing.
cues.reason: Callie perceives replenishment for the first time.

cues.delivery: Read the blankets, aligned boots, tucked laces, and watched breathing as evidence of painstaking care; never announce the sentiment.
cues.from: It was hot. She lay still and let the pump house put itself back together round her: the four grey walls, the roofless square of blue, the smell of old concrete and horse and somebody cooking something with onions. She was under two blankets she had not put on herself. Her boots were off. Somebody had pulled them off and stood them against the wall, side by side, with the laces tucked in, and she knew without needing to think about it that it had been her mother, left-handed, and that it had taken a long time.
cues.through: Callie lay and watched her breathe for a while. Then she got up.
cues.reason: The mother’s labor is inferred entirely through physical details.

cues.delivery: Let Pell’s denial of generosity remain ledger-dry; the humor conceals rather than cancels the value of what he has secured for her.
cues.from: "It's not a gift," said Pell. "It's a sum. I don't give gifts. I haven't the temperament." He turned a page back. "There's one other thing in there from last night, and you'll see it anyway if you read over my shoulder, which you do. So I'll show you."
cues.through: "It's not a gift," said Pell. "It's a sum. I don't give gifts. I haven't the temperament." He turned a page back. "There's one other thing in there from last night, and you'll see it anyway if you read over my shoulder, which you do. So I'll show you."
cues.reason: His character reveals care through accounting and denial.

cues.delivery: Give the ledger the dignity of a field record. Enunciate each fact without elegy, and close the book as the only burial Pell can provide.
cues.from: It was under the day's entry, under Causeway at dusk. C.'s call. Concur — K., P. Below that were four more lines in the same small hand, a little less neat than usual.
cues.through: C.'s call.
cues.reason: The mule’s death is mourned through duty and documentation.

cues.delivery: Read the ledger notation plainly and precisely as written initials, in the locked Calder base; no elegy or emotional swell.
cues.from: Concur — K., P.
cues.through: Concur — K., P.
cues.reason: A neutral document register preserves Pell's restrained bookkeeping and avoids forcing grief color into a three-word notation that repeatedly failed the naturalness floor.

cues.delivery: Give the ledger the dignity of a field record. Enunciate each fact without elegy, and close the book as the only burial Pell can provide.
cues.from: Below that were four more lines in the same small hand, a little less neat than usual.
cues.through: "Katori went and looked," he said. "It's where it went down. There's nothing to be done that'd be worth doing, and I won't have anybody going down that rock for anything less than an arrow." He closed the book. "That's all. I wanted it written. I've written it."
cues.reason: The mule’s death is mourned through duty and documentation.

cues.delivery: Keep Otto hesitant but exact: he is relieving Callie of blame with eyewitness fact, then restoring ordinary companionship through useful work.
cues.from: "She's sore," said Otto. He was sitting on the ground by the picket with his stitched arm in a sling made from one of Callie's mother's shirts, and a heap of harness across his knees that he was trying to mend one-handed. "The hind. Up here." He touched his own thigh. "Pell says she kicked so hard she hurt herself on it. He says it's like punching a wall." He paused, and looked at Callie, and then away. "He says it'll mend. He says she'll pull. Just not as well as before."
cues.through: Callie stood there a moment longer. Then she went and sat down on the gravel near him, but not too near, and began sorting the harness buckles into a pile. After a while, Otto passed her the end of a strap to hold, and she held it.
cues.reason: Practical reassurance allows Callie to remain near Duchess without forcing reconciliation.

cues.delivery: The words come too quickly because Callie has mistaken depletion for permanent loss; keep the panic contained inside precise statements.
cues.from: "It's gone," Callie said, before Katori could say anything. "Both of them. I went down and it's gone. There's nothing there."
cues.through: "It's gone," Callie said, before Katori could say anything. "Both of them. I went down and it's gone. There's nothing there."
cues.reason: Her private test produces the chapter’s last inward crisis.

cues.delivery: Katori admits ignorance without loss of steadiness, then makes partnership concrete; the slight mouth movement is restrained encouragement, not a smile played broadly.
cues.from: "I don't know how. I watched you get it off this morning with a barrow, and I didn't know how then either." Katori's mouth moved very slightly. "So we'll find out together. You and me. And you'll teach me, some of it, because you're the only one who's been inside it."

cues.reason: Mentor and student explicitly become collaborators.
